newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 30th July 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - 30th July 1997.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- BANK DEPUTY GOVERNOR NAMED

Dresdner Bank pre-empted the formal announcement of the Bank of England's appointment of Kleinwort Benson's vice-chairman David Clementi as the deputy governor responsible for financial stability. The Treasury was embarrassed at the premature announcement that Mr Clementi would be replacing Mr Howard Jones at the Bank of England who is to leave to join the expanded Securities and Investments Board.
-- BURGER KING PUT TO FLIGHT IN FRENCH FOOD WAR

UK-based food and drinks conglomerate Grand Metropolitan announced the closure of its 39 French branches of Burger King so that the company could target countries such as Spain, Germany and the UK where they had clear growth prospects. The move comes after the French chain of fast food outlets had long been struggling against competition because of its small presence and difficulties with profits which were reported as a loss of FFr126m on a turnover of FFr74m for 1996.
-- LARGE UK BOOKSTORES TO COMPETE ONLINE WITH US SITES

UK booksellers Dillons, part of entertainment group EMI, and the retailer W.H. Smith-owned Waterstone's announced their intention to launch 1m titles on internet sites in a bid to compete with big US online booksellers, a move which could possibly start a price war as both sites are expected to offer discounts on some titles. A similar situation occurred in the US when the Barnes and Noble book chain site, Amazon offered discounts up to 40 per cent and fears are now rising over Waterstones intention to sell the earlier- published US editions at its site.
-- BORROWING HITS RECORD LEVELS

The Bank of England reported that net consumer borrowing rose by 1.28bn stg in June compared to 1.23bn in May revealing the highest monthly figure since the series began in 1993 fuelling further acknowledgement of the need to increase interest rates again to stabilise the economy. The pound again fell for a second day to close down 3.1 pfennigs to DM2.983 which may stall interest rate rises for next month by the Bank of England.
-- BANK SET TO LOSE ROLE IN DEBT MANAGEMENT

In return for giving the Bank of England responsibility to set interest rates the government is to establish a new agency beginning next April to deal with the day-to-day management of the Exchequer's finance and the government debt. The Treasury announced that it was necessary to divide the debt management and interest rate operations of the Bank to ensure clearer distinctions between the two operations and so avoid conflicts of interest.
-- ONLINE PUB LOTTERIES FACE REVIEW

The minister responsible for gaming policy has told the Gaming Board that a government consultation will review the regulations concerning online lotteries following the Gaming Board's concern over Inter Lotto plans to launch a online lottery in pubs and shopping malls which has a draw every five minutes. The plans from the lottery firm chaired by Conservative peer Lord Mancroft sparked worries from the Gaming Board that pubs were not suitable venues for hard gambling.
-- COST AND SPEED DETER INTERNET USE

Technology and media research group Durlacher have released a survey report for British Telecommunications that shows only 17 per cent of households have ever used the internet with 91 per cent reporting awareness of the global network. Furthermore 35 per cent of households that have internet-compatible personnel computers are not online because of doubts about the price, accessibility and speed and delivery mechanisms.
-- ABBEY DISMISSES MERGER SPECULATION

Abbey National bank announced a 23 per cent increase in pre tax profit to 687m stg and dispelled speculation that the company was to merge with National Westminster Bank or the leading UK life assurer Prudential Corporation. Abbey's chairman Lord Tugendhat commented that the Bank had no intention to merge with a bank that has the burden of investments or an operation with an incongruous culture such as door-to-door sales.
-- GE CAPITAL AGREES 118M STG BID FOR CTR

General Electric subsidiary GE Capital has revealed that its 118m stg bid for the UK trailer rental company Central Transport Rental Group has been agreed sending CTR share prices souring 8.5p to 15.5p after the share bid of 16p was called. CTR's 238m stg debt is also to be taken on by GE Capital giving the firm an enterprise value in excess of 250m stg.
-- ADMIRAL LIFTED 39 PER CENT BY BUOYANT IT SECTOR DEMAND

Information technology services group Admiral reported a 39 per cent increase in pre-tax profit to 7.2m stg for the half year to June 30 thanks to strong underlying demand which lifted turnover 26 per cent to 54.1m stg including a 5.63m stg contribution from its last March acquisition of the French group Ares. Chairman Clay Brendish commented that the boom in the IT services industry has helped the company create 21 per cent more jobs in the firm which now has 1,800 employees.
